W1.name: Alder Valley
W1.identity: A stepped river valley with cedar houses, terraced fields, a stone viaduct, a bright rescue depot, and a mountain reservoir.
W1.thesis: Redirect water without transferring danger onto an evacuation route.
W1.aftercare: A repaired bridge carries the bus past a dry village square. The final postcard animates a river lantern festival.

W2.name: Emberwood
W2.identity: An inhabited forest reserve with a lookout tower, sawmill, campsite, orchard, and hillside water tanks.
W2.thesis: Create defensible transport routes by managing fuel, water, power, and forecast wind.
W2.aftercare: Rain arrives after stabilization, not as a deus ex machina that solves the mission. Residents replant the cleared strip.

W3.name: Frostline
W3.identity: A snow-covered alpine settlement with a funicular, weather observatory, cable station, avalanche fences, and steep terraces.
W3.thesis: Stabilize selected structures and schedule vertical rescue before runout paths close.
W3.aftercare: The funicular returns to service, carrying supplies rather than a compulsory victory cutscene.

W4.name: Tidemark
W4.identity: A fictional coastal archipelago with pale plaster houses, boatyards, a lighthouse, raised walkways, and a tidal market.
W4.thesis: Exploit safe tide windows and keep the power network dry while coordinating multiple transport legs.
W4.aftercare: The lighthouse sweeps across safe harbor and the floating market reopens.

W5.name: Cinder Reach
W5.identity: A volcanic island research town with basalt terraces, a geothermal station, orchards, a ferry terminal, and cooling channels.
W5.thesis: Trade temporary protection against permanent evacuation while slow hazards remove routes.
W5.aftercare: The rescue fleet leaves together; recovered residents send postcards from every earlier world.

W1-M1.title: First Crossing
W1-M1.decision: Learn bridge placement, flood forecasts, and a first boat route.
W1-M1.layout: Bus group of 4 at the west crossing; 4 residents at the low dock; depot and high landing are safe.

threats.text: Reservoir inflow increases
Low-dock water rises toward closure threshold
Final moderate surge tests the placed barrier

W1-M1.required: Evacuate at least 6 residents; deliver the bus group to the depot.
W1-M1.mastery: Rescue all 8 and keep the low dock usable until its group boards.
W1-M1.failure: Leaving the dock above the flood threshold too long closes boarding; backup transport recovers the unrescued group.
W1-M1.payoff: The first passengers turn and wave as the bridge unfolds.

W1-M2.title: The Lower Road
W1-M2.decision: Understand downstream consequences and dry power placement.
W1-M2.layout: Three groups of 4: orchard, river houses, and ferry landing; pump has two legal outlet regions.

threats.text: Rain begins in the upper basin
A warning reveals the lower-road closure forecast
Upper inflow peaks

W1-M2.required: Evacuate at least 9; maintain power at the medical station at mission end.
W1-M2.mastery: Rescue all 12 without exposing the orchard assembly point.
W1-M2.failure: An outlet into the orchard transfers the hazard to waiting residents; debrief displays the actual flow path.
W1-M2.payoff: A pumping hose visibly bulges while a previously flooded road reappears.

W1-M3.title: Two Banks
W1-M3.decision: Allocate transport capacity between separated groups.
W1-M3.layout: West village has 8 residents; east workshop 6. One bridge socket connects only the high paths, not both docks.

threats.text: A central surge closes the low footpath
Debris blocks one boat lane after a clear warning
The east landing becomes the shorter remaining route

W1-M3.required: Evacuate at least 11; empty the east workshop group.
W1-M3.mastery: Rescue all 14 with no idle fully loaded skiff at the end.
W1-M3.failure: A boat assigned to a closing lane waits at a safe node; the player must reassign it.
W1-M3.payoff: Two boats cross beneath the viaduct carrying different rescue groups.

W1-M4.title: Power Before Water
W1-M4.decision: Trade early protection against immediate evacuation.
W1-M4.layout: Clinic, tram depot, and riverside housing share a power bottleneck. Dry source sockets are scarce but sufficient.

threats.text: First spill enters the clinic basin
Tram passengers reach the assembly point
One low connection shuts down unless protected
Final spill threatens the second basin

W1-M4.required: Evacuate at least 12; preserve the clinic power connection at end.
W1-M4.mastery: Rescue all 16 while keeping both generators operational.
W1-M4.failure: Overcommitting power leaves a pump queued; the UI names the inactive consumer.
W1-M4.payoff: The town’s lights return in a visible chain when power is restored.

W1-M5.title: The Long Way Home
W1-M5.decision: Combine flow, power, routing, and a deliberate equipment tradeoff.
W1-M5.layout: Four groups of 5 occupy the upper village, orchard, workshop, and island landing. Three elevations create alternate safe routes.

threats.text: First surge reveals the main fork
A forecast landslide closes the short road
Reservoir overflow increases source flow
Late inflow tests the downstream basin

W1-M5.required: Evacuate at least 15; restore a continuous route between depot and upper village.
W1-M5.mastery: Rescue all 20 and finish with no stranded loaded vehicle.
W1-M5.failure: A poor early diversion consumes safe basin capacity and forces a longer evacuation; no instant unannounced loss.
W1-M5.payoff: The final bus and skiff arrive together while the town’s rescue bell rings.

W2-M1.title: A Line in the Trees
W2-M1.layout: Campsite and lookout connect through two wooded paths; one tank supplies both sprinkler sockets.

threats.text: A marked dry-cell cluster ignites
Steady wind advances heat toward the short path
The first cooled strip becomes safe to cross

W2-M1.required: Rescue at least 8; preserve a path to the lookout.
W2-M1.mastery: Rescue all 10 while retaining water in the tank.
W2-M1.failure: A gap in the firebreak permits predictable spread.
W2-M1.payoff: The fire stops along the exact strip the player cleared.

W2-M2.title: Last Bus from Camp
W2-M2.layout: Three camps each hold 6 people; two road loops meet at a refill station.

threats.text: One road becomes threatened
A wind warning marks the alternate loop
The refill station approaches heat threshold

W2-M2.required: Rescue at least 14; unload every occupied crawler before finishing.
W2-M2.mastery: Rescue all 18 without losing the refill station.
W2-M2.failure: An empty vehicle on the wrong loop costs time but can be rerouted.
W2-M2.payoff: Campers board with tiny backpacks and return a lost flag.

W2-M3.title: Water Is a Route
W2-M3.decision: Make water supply and transport choices interact.
W2-M3.layout: A pond and storage tank feed separate areas; a pump link can refill the tank without protecting the road by itself.

threats.text: Orchard edge heats
The tank drops below half unless replenished
A second ignition threatens the return road

W2-M3.required: Rescue at least 12; keep the orchard assembly route usable.
W2-M3.mastery: Rescue all 16 with neither water source exhausted.
W2-M3.failure: A sprinkler without water shows a visible dry gauge rather than pretending to operate.
W2-M3.payoff: A hose network creates a brief corridor through a glowing forest edge.

W2-M4.title: When the Wind Turns
W2-M4.layout: Four groups use a road network with two dominant wind-exposed edges; a fixed powered tank is provided.

threats.text: Wind is stable westward
A 40-second warning precedes an eastward turn
A second turn threatens the unprotected flank

W2-M4.required: Rescue at least 15; empty the lookout group.
W2-M4.mastery: Rescue all 20 without rebuilding a committed firebreak.
W2-M4.failure: Ignoring the visible wind timeline makes the formerly safe flank dangerous.
W2-M4.payoff: Leaves and smoke lean before the route warning changes.

W2-M5.title: The Green Corridor
W2-M5.decision: Maintain a living evacuation corridor through a combined burn.
W2-M5.layout: Campsite, orchard, and sawmill each hold 8; two water tanks and one long safe route can support a coordinated solution.

threats.text: Outer forest ignition
Sawmill access becomes threatened
Wind shifts toward the central route
Final heat peak reaches the corridor flank

W2-M5.required: Rescue at least 18; preserve the central route at end.
W2-M5.mastery: Rescue all 24 and save the orchard pump house.
W2-M5.failure: Protecting every decorative building leaves too little transport capacity.
W2-M5.payoff: The last crawler exits as residents begin planting the first new sapling.

W3-M1.title: Hold the Station
W3-M1.decision: Introduce structure-specific support and vertical transfers.
W3-M1.layout: Two terraces connect at the cable station; one known weak support threatens the link.

threats.text: A support begins losing stability
Meltwater increases load
A minor tremor tests bracing

W3-M1.required: Rescue at least 8; preserve the cable support.
W3-M1.mastery: Rescue all 10 with no station shutdown.
W3-M1.failure: Bracing decorative rocks has no effect; only eligible supports accept placement.
W3-M1.payoff: Cable tension relaxes visibly when a brace locks into place.

W3-M2.title: Above the Snowline
W3-M2.decision: Manage independent rescue links and power.
W3-M2.layout: Three terraces; two winch links and one sheltered intermediate node.

threats.text: Upper path closes under snow
Sheltered node receives an arriving group
One unbraced cable platform approaches instability

W3-M2.required: Rescue at least 11; empty the top observatory.
W3-M2.mastery: Rescue all 14 without trapping residents at the intermediate node.
W3-M2.failure: Moving people uphill into a temporary staging node without onward capacity blocks the route.
W3-M2.payoff: Tiny lights descend the mountain in two synchronized lifts.

W3-M3.title: The Quiet Slope
W3-M3.decision: Read runout zones and preserve a secondary route.
W3-M3.layout: A broad slope threatens one road; a rock shelf provides a longer bypass.

threats.text: Slope stability warning appears
A marked avalanche runout closes the short road
Cooling makes one debris edge clearable in the authored route

W3-M3.required: Rescue at least 12; evacuate the weather crew.
W3-M3.mastery: Rescue all 16 without entering the marked runout during release.
W3-M3.failure: A closed road stops vehicles at a safe node; it does not fling rigidbody residents.
W3-M3.payoff: A soft wall of stylized snow follows the warned corridor exactly.

W3-M4.title: Cable and Current
W3-M4.decision: Combine snow support and flooding power platforms.
W3-M4.layout: A warming lower basin threatens generators while upper cables carry residents.

threats.text: Lower snowmelt starts
Cable load increases
A second meltwater source activates

W3-M4.required: Rescue at least 14; keep one complete powered cable route available at end.
W3-M4.mastery: Rescue all 18 while keeping both lower platforms dry.
W3-M4.failure: Ignoring the lower basin breaks a logically correct upper rescue plan.
W3-M4.payoff: A small stream passes beneath the rescued cable line rather than over its power box.

W3-M5.title: Dawn at Frostline
W3-M5.layout: Observatory, station, and village groups converge through limited safe terraces.

threats.text: Forecast warming begins
First cable support warning
Runout closes the valley shortcut
Final transport window opens at the lower station

W3-M5.required: Rescue at least 17; clear the observatory and station groups.
W3-M5.mastery: Rescue all 22 with no occupied vehicle or shelter left behind.
W3-M5.failure: Using the receiving station as indefinite storage causes a capacity bottleneck.
W3-M5.payoff: The sun reaches the restored station as the last cabin arrives.

W4-M1.title: Between Two Tides
W4-M1.layout: Two islands connect by a low causeway and an all-tide boat route; a fixed dry source powers the receiving dock.

threats.text: Tide begins rising
Causeway closes
High landing becomes optimal for unloading

W4-M1.required: Rescue at least 9; clear the low-market group.
W4-M1.mastery: Rescue all 12 without a loaded boat waiting at a closed dock.
W4-M1.failure: An incorrect dock remains visible but rejects loading with a tide explanation.
W4-M1.payoff: Market umbrellas fold as the water reaches the tide ruler.

W4-M2.title: Keep the Light
W4-M2.decision: Keep a dry power route while transporting residents.
W4-M2.layout: Three elevated relay sockets can route around a flood-prone connection to the lighthouse.

threats.text: Low cable channel floods
Receiving dock needs lighthouse power for its safe route signal
Peak tide threatens the shortest relay path

W4-M2.required: Rescue at least 12; power the lighthouse at end.
W4-M2.mastery: Rescue all 16 with no power outage during final unloading.
W4-M2.failure: Moving a relay while its only route is actively required temporarily blocks unloading.
W4-M2.payoff: A lighthouse beam returns exactly when the circuit closes.

W4-M3.title: The Floating Market
W4-M3.decision: Handle multiple pickups and staging capacity.
W4-M3.layout: Four markets each hold 5; the safe island has limited docks but sufficient total refuge.

threats.text: First tidal lane opens
A stall pontoon blocks one marked channel
Current direction favors the outer loop

W4-M3.required: Rescue at least 15; unload all occupied skiffs.
W4-M3.mastery: Rescue all 20 without exceeding any staging node capacity.
W4-M3.failure: Assigning all boats to one dock creates a readable queue, not overlapping models.
W4-M3.payoff: Boats line up between colorful awnings and a miniature harbor crane.

W4-M4.title: Storm Switch
W4-M4.decision: Combine rain inflow and sea-level changes.
W4-M4.layout: Rain fills an inland basin while tide threatens pump outlets and the power network.

threats.text: Rain source starts
Tide reduces discharge efficiency
A brief low-tide window opens
Final rain peak

W4-M4.required: Rescue at least 17; keep the medical landing accessible at end.
W4-M4.mastery: Rescue all 22 without pumping into the occupied market basin.
W4-M4.failure: A pump outlet submerged under a tide has reduced effect, clearly shown in its forecast.
W4-M4.payoff: Two different water levels become visible across the barrier line.

W4-M5.title: Harbor of Everyone
W4-M5.decision: Master transport, tide windows, and power topology.
W4-M5.layout: Three islands, two causeways, four pickup groups, and a lighthouse-backed safe harbor.

threats.text: Rising tide closes the first causeway
Power warning at the harbor
Outer route becomes faster with the current
Last high-water phase closes low docks

W4-M5.required: Rescue at least 20; restore lighthouse power and empty every temporary staging dock.
W4-M5.mastery: Rescue all 26 with the high causeway still usable.
W4-M5.failure: Saving the lighthouse alone cannot satisfy the rescue goal.
W4-M5.payoff: The harbor fills with rescued boats under a single calm sweep of light.

W5-M1.title: A Path Through Heat
W5-M1.layout: Two heat channels divide an orchard from a high landing; one shelter socket lies outside the permanent safe zone.

threats.text: Lava advances into a marked channel
First cooling opportunity appears
Cooled segment begins reheating

W5-M1.required: Rescue at least 9; empty the temporary shelter before completion.
W5-M1.mastery: Rescue all 12 before the first crossing reheats.
W5-M1.failure: Cooling too early wastes the safe window; the timer remains visible.
W5-M1.payoff: A black crust forms under a cooling plume and opens a narrow path.

W5-M2.title: Borrowed Safety
W5-M2.decision: Use refuge as a temporary logistics tool, not a destination.
W5-M2.layout: Two groups need protection while the crawler travels between sectors.

threats.text: Heat advances toward the first assembly point
Shelter protection starts being consumed
The outer route opens after a cooling phase

W5-M2.required: Rescue at least 14; both temporary shelters empty at end.
W5-M2.mastery: Rescue all 18 without exhausting a shelter protection interval.
W5-M2.failure: Leaving residents in shelters fails the evacuation condition even if they remain safe.
W5-M2.payoff: Shelter lamps change state as the last group boards the crawler.

W5-M3.title: The Cooling Works
W5-M3.layout: A cooling plant supplies finite coolant; water drainage protects its generator and relay.

threats.text: Drainage basin begins filling
Heat threatens coolant delivery
A second channel cuts the default route

W5-M3.required: Rescue at least 15; keep the cooling works available at end.
W5-M3.mastery: Rescue all 20 while retaining one coolant charge.
W5-M3.failure: Power loss stops production but does not erase stored coolant.
W5-M3.payoff: The plant’s pipes light in sequence and a safe corridor opens.

W5-M4.title: Three Ways Out
W5-M4.decision: Choose among sea, road, and temporary crossings.
W5-M4.layout: Three sectors support different transport types; all routes share limited final receiving capacity.

threats.text: Road warning
Heat closes the short land route
Sea route improves as debris clears
Final cooling window

W5-M4.required: Rescue at least 18; clear the research crew and all temporary refuge.
W5-M4.mastery: Rescue all 24 with no stranded vehicle load.
W5-M4.failure: Overloading one final landing creates a queue; capacity indicators must predict it.
W5-M4.payoff: A boat and crawler transfer groups at the same tiny pier.

W5-M5.title: Every Little Life
W5-M5.decision: Final combined-system rescue with meaningful priorities.
W5-M5.layout: Five groups of 6 span an orchard, station, research terraces, waterfront, and high village. No new mechanic is introduced.

threats.text: Rain and heat begin in separate regions
First transport route warning
Generator platform needs drainage
Last heat front approaches the staging zone

W5-M5.required: Rescue at least 23; empty all temporary shelters and restore the final ferry route.
W5-M5.mastery: Rescue all 30 without any equipment loss.
W5-M5.failure: A plan that protects scenery but delays evacuation cannot earn a successful outcome.
W5-M5.payoff: Every rescued group joins a single departure; the credits can be skipped without interrupting the final save.
